newsitem.title: USA: U.S. can grow faster without a looser Fed - Lindsey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. can grow faster without a looser Fed - Lindsey.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey on Friday said the U.S. economy is capable of growing faster over the long term but he stressed that lax monetary policy was not the means for achieving that.
"I do believe the American economy can grow quicker and that the American people are right in demanding that it do so," Lindsey said in a speech to the Atlantic Economic Conference.
"Rather than resort to the age-old palliative of printing money, our leaders must turn their sights onto those things for which they are directly responsible," he said.
Lindsey pointed to the public sector as the area where the greatest impediments to growth existed.
Specifically, he listed the failures of public education, problems with entitlement programs and inefficiencies in the way government allocates resources as the main barriers to growth.
Looking at entitlement programs, the Fed governor said public-sector retirement and health-care programs were impeding capital formation.
On the issue of how government allocates its resources, Lindsey said curbing government borrowing by raising taxes was not the way to boost the U.S. savings rate, which he said was too low.
One important goal for public policy would be to address how efficiently capital and labor are used in the economy, he said.
Concerning the role of monetary policy in furthering long-term growth, the Fed official said its most important contribution would be to maintain stability and hold down inflation.

"While monetary policy cannot influence the amount of labor or capital available to the economy in any sustainable way, it probably can help augment growth by improving the way resources are used," Lindsey said.
"I believe that the best pro-growth prescription is to let monetary policy run in a stable, predictable fashion which involves little or no inflation," he said.
